newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury boosts Xmas sales, profits hurt.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury boosts Xmas sales, profits hurt.

text.p: British supermarket retailer J. Sainsbury Plc warned on Friday that pretax profits would be hit hard this year and would be around 640-650 million pounds before a 50 million pound charge but reported key Christmas sales from same stores rose 4.4 percent.
"We are disappointed that the costs of building sales across the businesses have impacted group profit," chairman David Sainsbury said in a statement.

According to the Estimate Directory, previous consensus forecast on full year pretax profits was around 760 million pounds ($1.24 billion) and Sainsbury said that "costs of rebuilding sales momentum have reduced profitability in the short term."
Arch-rival Tesco, which pushed Sainsbury off the market leader slot a year ago, said earlier this week that its Christmas sales from existing stores were up 7.5 percent.

Sainsbury said same store sales in the 16 weeks to January 11 were up four percent at its supermarkkets, just ahead of inflation at three percent, giving it positive volume growth, adding that 80 percent of sales used its loyalty card of which there are now over eight million in issue.

Sainsbury said that despite an extremely competitive food retailing market, gross margins had remained stable and that management was now focused "on turning increased sales into profit growth." ($1=.6119 Pound)
